errors: One commit (b010a8e72) swept in the jwt auditor's half-written audit file (invalid JSON) because I ran git add on the audits directory while an auditor was still writing; the next commit replaced it with the validated version before merge.

doc_friction.issue: Parallel auditors write into the shared audits/ directory; nothing warns the lead not to git add the directory until every auditor has reported. Committing per file by name avoids it.
'Load the served page at https://marisstella.app/<slug>/' cannot be done from cloud sessions: all three auditors got a proxy 403 / ENOTFOUND, so served-page checks were recorded as partial.

The pkill hook also refuses a command where the bracketed pattern text appears elsewhere on the line (for example in the command that started the server); kill $! is simpler for a server you started yourself.

deviations.why: Step 4 scopes fixes to the audited subjects; the jwt XSS pattern was a family defect, so I scanned all venture pages and fixed the two sister paste-and-check tools (mcp-config-risk-check, skill-manifest-check) whose pasted input reached innerHTML.
deviations.did: Fixed both with page tests, confirmed old page vulnerable and new page safe in headless Chromium.
deviations.result: Two more live XSS bugs closed; 12 lower-risk scan hits listed below, unreviewed.

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
